entities.evidence: Seth fathers Enosh here, matching Adam and Eve’s son Seth, whose son is named Enosh in Genesis 4:26.
Enosh is the son Seth fathers here, the same father and son named in Genesis 4:26.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁת is the subject, and חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה gives the duration. Seth lived 105 years before he fathered Enosh.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and shortened verb form יְחִי.
analysis.sense: to live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: שֵׁת is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived,” and וַיּוֹלֶד, “he fathered.” The verse identifies Seth as the father of Enosh at age 105.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the son of Adam and his wife born after Abel’s death

analysis.evidence: חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים means “five years.” The following וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adds a hundred years, giving Seth’s age as 105 when he fathered Enosh.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים means “five years.” Together with וּמְאַת שָׁנָה (“and a hundred years”), it gives Seth’s age of 105 when he fathered Enosh.
מְאַת governs שָׁנָה in וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, “and a hundred years.” The conjunction adds those years to חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים, “five years,” giving Seth’s age as 105 when he fathered Enosh.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ prefixed to מְאַת, the singular construct form of the cardinal numeral מֵאָה.

analysis.evidence: In וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, the singular שָׁנָה supplies the unit counted by מְאַת, “a hundred.” Together with חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים, “five years,” the phrase gives Seth’s age of 105 when he fathered Enosh.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁת (Seth) remains the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and אֶת marks אֱנוֹשׁ (Enosh) as its direct object. Seth fathered Enosh at the age of 105.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת אֱנוֹשׁ “he fathered Enosh,” אֶת marks the personal name אֱנוֹשׁ as the direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Seth is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד ‘he fathered’, and אֶת marks אֱנוֹשׁ as its direct object. Enosh names the son Seth fathered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix
